passage: Sunday, late. I slipped this weekend. Saturday and most of Sunday went on videos, and I feel low about it. But I've decided not to be horrible to myself, because that never helped. Instead I asked what set it off. First there was the argument with my brother on Friday, which left me angry and restless. Then there was nothing planned, so the empty hours filled up. That's two triggers: a fight and boredom. So here's what changes: next Saturday I've asked my friend Keerthana to go to the market with me, something fixed and outside. And tomorrow I start again as normal. One bad weekend doesn't cancel the two good weeks. — Rekha

qa.q: What set off the weekend of videos?
qa.a: An argument with a brother and having nothing planned.

qa.q: How does Rekha feel about the slip, and how is it handled?
qa.a: Low and disappointed, but Rekha chooses to be kind to self instead of harsh, and looks for triggers.

qa.q: What else could Rekha do to prepare for boring stretches, and why?
qa.a: Keep a short list of things to do when bored, since a ready list is easier to use than deciding on the spot.

qa.q: How does the outing look to Keerthana?
qa.a: Keerthana, invited to the market, may feel glad to be included and to help a friend get through a hard weekend.

grounding: After a weekend slip, a student checks the triggers, plans an outing for next weekend and restarts the next day.

passage:
Madhav: so my screen plan died this weekend
Trisha: how bad
Madhav: 9 hrs saturday. 7 sunday 😬
Trisha: ok. what happened before it started
Madhav: had a fight with my dad friday night. then saturday nothing to do, everyone was out
Trisha: so angry + bored
Madhav: yeah. i was going to quit the whole plan tbh
Trisha: or just start again tomorrow. one bad weekend isn't the whole plan
Madhav: true. and weekends are clearly the weak spot
Trisha: so plan the weekend. come to the lake cycling thing saturday? 7 am
Madhav: ok yes. and i'll talk to dad tonight, properly this time
Madhav: back on the plan from monday. i mean tomorrow. it IS monday tomorrow 😅
Trisha: perfect

qa.q: How many hours did Madhav spend on screens on Saturday?
What feelings came before the binge, according to the chat?
qa.a: Madhav was angry after the fight with his dad, and then bored with everyone out.

qa.q: What will Madhav change for next weekend?
qa.a: Plan the weak spot with the Saturday lake cycling, and talk to his dad properly so the anger doesn't carry over.

qa.q: How does Trisha see the bad weekend?
qa.a: Trisha treats it as information, not failure, asking what came before and offering a plan instead of judging.

grounding: Shows a student looking at what triggered a weekend binge, an argument and boredom, planning an outing for next weekend and restarting the next day.

passage:
On Monday morning in Nabha, Mehak looked at the weekend's screen-time number and felt the old urge: that's it, I'm hopeless, why even try. Eleven hours on Sunday alone.
Instead she sat on the steps behind the family shop with her notebook, the way her plan said to, and asked two questions: what happened just before, and what can I change?
Saturday afternoon, she and Ammi had argued about the college form, and she'd gone to her room fuming. Sunday, the power was out most of the day, her cousin Gautam had gone to the fair without her, and there was nothing to do but lie there with the phone.
So: a fight, then boredom. She wrote down next Sunday's plan: the gurdwara kitchen with Gautam in the morning, helping at the shop in the afternoon. She texted Gautam to make sure he'd wait for her.
Then she went back to Monday's plan, just as before.

qa.q: Where is Mehak going with Gautam next Sunday morning?
What was Mehak feeling when she first saw the weekend number?
qa.a: She felt discouraged and hopeless, with the old urge to give up entirely.

qa.q: Why is asking "what happened just before" more useful than blaming herself?
qa.a: It reveals the triggers, the argument and the boredom, so she can plan around them instead of just feeling bad.

qa.q: How might Gautam see Mehak's message about next Sunday?
qa.a: Gautam may feel a little guilty for going to the fair alone, and glad to be included this time.

grounding: Shows a student checking what triggered a weekend binge, an argument and boredom, planning a busy next Sunday, and restarting the next day.
